tested_condition: Authority-derived tokens are adapted into reusable global design foundations for the Next.js application shell.
expected_outcome: Shared color, typography, spacing, radius, shadow, container, and breakpoint tokens exist in implementation-accessible locations.
actual_outcome: Authority-derived tokens were materialized into app/globals.css and lib/design-tokens.ts, preserving the approved light editorial system while adapting it to reusable application primitives.
passes: Global CSS variables now reflect the authority's light neutral background, muted ink, violet accent, mono kicker, and surface hierarchy.
Type, spacing, container, radius, and shadow tokens were centralized for later page materialization.
Token usage supports mobile-first layout collapse and accessible focus visibility.

typography_tokens.label: 0.75rem
typography_tokens.font_display: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, SF Pro Display, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif
typography_tokens.font_body: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, SF Pro Text, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif
typography_tokens.font_mono: ui-monospace, JetBrains Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

breakpoint_strategy.implementation_note: Phase 2 implementation keeps core breakpoints at 430px and 768px while preserving room for additional page-specific thresholds in Phase 3.

mobile_first_strategy: Base styles assume narrow viewports; header, nav, card-grid, and CTA action wrapping progressively expand at larger breakpoints.
accessibility_considerations: Visible 3px focus ring preserved from design authority intent.
Tap targets and action controls are kept at or above 44px minimum height.
Muted text remains separated from body text by hierarchy and spacing rather than reduced size alone.
Reduced-motion handling disables long transitions and smooth scrolling.
